reviews.text: Friendly and reasonable prices.  Takes care of my dogs.

I initially believed this place deserved a better rating. My first visit went well and I left with a positive impression. Unfortunately, that visit was followed by one of the hardest decisions we’ve ever had to make: putting our pup down.

Yesterday I returned to pick up my dog’s cremated remains, after already spending a considerable amount of money with this business. Obviously, returning to this place was difficult enough without being treated the way I was.

The front door had an “Open” sign displayed but was locked. The side entrance also had an “Open” sign. I went through that entrance because I had used it during my previous visit and actually completed my transaction through that same door. I had no reason to think it was inappropriate to enter through there, especially with the front entrance locked and both doors displaying “Open” signs.

After the receptionist finished her phone call, I said hello. Before I could explain why I was there, she abruptly said, “Yeah, you’re not supposed to come in through there.” I explained that the front door was locked and that I assumed this was the available entrance. Before I could finish, she interrupted me again: “Yeah, well, we have it locked for a reason, and you’re not supposed to come in through this side.”

I finally explained that I was there to pick up my dog’s remains. Her response was a rude and inconvenienced, “Yeah, again, I… I don’t know. I don’t know where that would be. I don’t have any information.” She eventually found my pet, who was only a few steps away.

I understand that people have bad days, but this was an especially inappropriate way to treat someone returning to a place where they experienced a heartbreaking loss. This wasn’t just a random interaction. I was there to pick up my dog after paying this business a significant amount of money for their services.

Her attitude bothered me enough that I later called to tell her that she could have communicated the situation better and that I felt she had been hostile. Instead of de-escalating, she responded, “I can get hostile if that’s what you want.”

I asked for her name because I felt a formal complaint was appropriate. She responded, “I don’t have to give you that, and I don’t need to do this with you.”

This interaction left me wondering what the attitude toward customers is like behind closed doors. If this is how comfortable someone is speaking to a customer directly, it makes you wonder how customers are spoken about when they aren’t standing there.

To the owner: please address this. A business dealing with people and their beloved pets requires humanity, patience, and grace. People come to you during some of the hardest moments of their lives. They shouldn’t have to deal with hostility and unnecessary attitude on top of that. I’ve genuinely had better service at the DMV.

I am especially disappointed because my initial experience was good. I wanted to believe this was a business that genuinely cared about its customers and their pets. After this interaction, I no longer feel that way.

To anyone reading this, I’m not exaggerating what happened. If your pet is going through a difficult situation, consider whether compassionate and respectful customer service matters to you before choosing where to go. The situation is already hard enough.

I gave this business my money and my trust during an incredibly difficult time. After this interaction, I don’t feel that either was respected. 0 stars if I could. One star is far too generous.

Someone with common sense would lock the employee entrance and leave the main entrance open! AM I RIGHT!?? Anyway he explained that to the lady in front and she explained how "HOSTILE" she can get before trying to understand the situation he asked for her name she simple replied "I don’t have to give you that" okay sure! But this couple is picking up their dead pet family pet might I add and giving this vet their business with cash money! Is that how you treat your grieving customers? Shitty receptionist shitty Doctor and shitty customer service! Do not take your pet here unless you want to be greeted with Hostility and Rude responses. Imagine what they say about the pets and their owners behind closed doors!

My recent experience at Alamo Cat and Dog Vet revealed several areas that need significant improvement. While the clinic seems almost perpetually busy, likely an indicator of being understaffed, this has unfortunately led to a noticeable decline in service efficiency and organization.

During my last visit, the **triage process was chaotic and disorganized**.The triage staff's overall flow was confusing, leading to unnecessary delays and a sense of disarray. This disorganization was further underscored by the fact that **a client ahead of me in the queue was completely overlooked by the front desk**, despite waiting for a considerable amount of time. This kind of lapse in basic customer service is unacceptable and speaks to a clear issue with managing patient flow, especially when the clinic is busy.

While I appreciate the care for animals, the operational inefficiencies and evident understaffing are creating a less than ideal experience for pet owners. Improvements in front desk management and patient intake procedures are crucial for a more positive and less stressful visit.

I was referred from Blue Cross Pet Clinic to Pleasanton Road Animal Hospital in the best interest of my kitten Daffy. Dr. Beissner wanted the best possible success for Daffy’s hip surgery. He is about 3 months old and got hit by a car. After all tests were done, it was determined he would need surgery for both his hip and his tail. Both staff and Dr. Pamplin were so helpful and caring. It’s very hard to find such caring vets that in the end really want to help all pet owners including those of us that may not have the highest income. I trusted Dr. Beissner’s recommendation after he cared for another cat of mine. And both have this same frame of mind. If it weren’t for how far this clinic is to my home, I would do all vet care here with them. Please don’t hesitate to call. They are honest and caring. Both staff and Dr. Pamplin. Daffy is doing great and I couldn’t have asked for better care. In fact Dr. Pamplin will not go with surgery if your pet is not doing well health wise, which was Daffy’s case. He still had worms and fleas and was anemic. They sent us home with meds and treatment plan and rescheduled surgery. I am glad they were honest. Daffy was much better and stronger after this treatment and did well with his surgery. This clinic may not be fancy but has the most important things, caring staff with a great vet who understand we aren’t rich either.

Took my cat here for routine vaccinations and happily returned to get his dental cleaning done. Dr. Pamplin is knowledgeable, costs are up front and reasonable, and it's obvious that the staff here cares about their clients.
